items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: So 80 percent of what say Sonny Rollins does is from his eyes.

ctx.x: I’m going to see if I can focus on that statement which you’ve said a couple of times, in that you didn’t know what you were doing. Can you tell me, is it sort of like I’m playing this note and I really like it so I’m going to hang on it, but what I don’t know is its relationship to the chord? Can you just talk about that a little bit?

Well you know 80 percent of what I do is from my ear. So 80 percent of what say Sonny Rollins does is from his eyes. He can see things and play — well Pee Wee Ellis. Pee Wee Ellis is a great example. He sees what he can hear. I hear what I can make music from. I could hear things that he can see from looking at it you know. But it was a natural thing with me. But if you write it out, I’m lost. Because I don’t know where — I say well let me hear it. And then they play it and I say, “Okay I’m going to do that.” You…
difference between what I do and what most musicians do. Most musicians can see and hear, but I can only hear. I can only hear what’s happening. You know?
